plain_text:
The National Institutes of Health (NIH)—the nation’s medical research agency—includes 27 Institutes and Centers and is
a part of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. It is the primary federal agency for conducting and supporting
basic, clinical, and translational medical research, and it investigates the causes, treatments, and cures for both common and
rare diseases. For more information about NIH and its programs, visit www.nih.gov.
